comment: Crop cycles and nutrition follow the CSA Interplanetary Farming planning values as summarised in api info/Luna_Academy_Food_Production_Research.md. kcal/m² and water figures are simulation values derived from those planning ranges, not measured lunar yields. The greenhouse is sealed: no direct sunlight, no unshielded radiation, light from colony power, CO2 from the cabin, water from storage.

crops.note: CSA 21–28 days. Vitamins K, A and C. Fast early harvest; salad and morale. Current grow-pod crop.
CSA 45–65 days. Protein, fats, calcium, iron, folate. Needs boiling in shell.
CSA 50–90 days. Vitamins A, C and K, fibre. Fresh food and variety; needs pollination support.
CSA 70–80 days. Vitamin A, potassium, fibre. Storage-friendly; roots need growing volume.
CSA 80 days fresh, 100 days dried. Protein, fibre, iron, folate.
CSA 90–170 days. High edible value but a long cycle for a 30-day mission.
CSA about 75 days. Herb for flavour and menu variety.
CSA about 90 days. Herb and food-variety crop.
CSA 213–244 days. Staple, but needs grinding equipment and outlasts a 30-day mission.
